elements.name: question12
elements.html:
Phase: 1

 

Purpose and Study Drug

 

This study is investigating a potential new treatment for acquired hypothalamic obesity, a condition that can develop due to genetic defects or injury to the hypothalamus, a region of the brain involved in regulating hunger and body weight. The condition is characterised by extreme hunger and rapid or progressive weight gain.

 

The treatment is being studied in healthy volunteers first to help researchers understand its safety and how it behaves in the body before it is tested in people living with the condition.

elements.name: question7
elements.html:
Note for recruiters: This study will run a bit differently to the usual SAD cohorts of a HV study.

 

There will be 2 main groups (S1 and S2), they will be alternately dose levels and in-clinic stays. Each group will receive 4 different doses.

elements.name: question13
elements.html:
Study Design

 

Participants will be randomly allocated to receive oral tablets or capsules containing either the study drug or a placebo. This study is double-blinded, meaning neither you nor the study staff will know which group you are allocated to until the study finishes.

 

If you are eligible following this phone pre-screen, you will attend the clinic for screening assessments. These include blood tests, vital signs, ECGs and a physical examination to confirm eligibility.

 

Participants in this study will receive the study drug on four occasions. Each occasion will involve a 3-night in-clinic stay, for a total of four separate stays (12 nights in total). The study drug will be administered following the first night of each stay.

 

After the final in-clinic stay, participants will complete 12 follow-up phone calls.

 

There are two main groups we are recruiting for. Participants must be available for all possible dates within their chosen group, there is no leeway from Period 2 onwards. We will be booking PTs into Sentinel or ROC in Period 1 as we would normally do for a HV study.

 

SAD Cohort S1 Period 1 [Sentinel is filled, pls book ROC only]

Your in-clinic stay will fall on the 30th of November - 3rd of December (ROC)

 

SAD Cohort S1 Period 2

Your in-clinic stay will fall on either the 5th - 8th of January or the 6th - 9th of January.

 

SAD Cohort S1 Period 3

Your in-clinic stay will fall on either the 8th - 11th of February or the 9th - 12th of February.

 

SAD Cohort S1 Period 4

Your in-clinic stay will fall on either the 14th - 17th of March or the 15th - 18th of March.

 

or

 

SAD Cohort S2 Period 1

Your in-clinic stay will fall on either the 14th - 17th of December (Sentinel) or the 15th - 18th of December (ROC). Pls get PT to chose which dates for Period 1 works best for them and book into Sent or ROC as applicable. Note: it is only Period 1 that PT's will get this option

 

SAD Cohort S2 Period 2

Your in-clinic stay will fall on either the 21st - 24th of January or the 24th - 27th of January.

 

SAD Cohort S2 Period 3

Your in-clinic stay will fall on either the 24th - 27th of February or the 25th - 28th of February.

 

SAD Cohort S2 Period 4

Your in-clinic stay will fall on either the 31st of March - 3rd of April or the 1st - 4th of April.

 

 

Could you please confirm your availability for these dates? We would only be able to offer you a screening appointment if you would be able to make the above dates.

elements.name: question14
elements.html:
Reimbursement

 

You will receive a set reimbursement amount for your participation in this research study. This reimbursement is inclusive of travel, parking, meals, and any other expenses associated with study visits; these are not paid separately

 

  • Screening visit: $300
  • Admission and discharge days: $240
  • Overnight stay: $480 per night
  • Follow-up phone call: $100
  • Unscheduled visits: $300
  • Retention bonus (if all study visits are completed): $500
  • Eligible alternate: $780

 

Thus, if you complete the entire study, you will receive a payment of approx. $6,760.

 

If you are an eligible alternate*, and do not get dosed, you will receive a partial reimbursement of $780.

*To make sure there are enough participants ready for dosing on Day 1, extra volunteers, called 'alternates', will also be recruited and admitted. On Day 1, before the study drug is given, your study participation status will be confirmed. If you are an alternate, you might be included in the study if a participant from the dosing group is unable to proceed.

elements.name: question26
elements.title: Do you have any medical conditions or significant medical history?

elements.name: question27
elements.html:
As mentioned, we are looking for healthy participants.

If participants have a medical condition but it does not require treatment, you may want to pose a doctor enquiry. 

If medical condition requires treatment with daily medication, please exclude as the study DOES NOT ALLOW prescription medication within the past 7 days prior to dosing!

 

Please always exclude the following:

  • clinically significant renal, hepatic, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, respiratory, haematologic, dermatologic, autoimmune, endocrine (PCOS that doesn't require treatment is okay), inflammatory, neurological, psychiatric disease, or any uncontrolled medical condition
  • current or recent infection within 14 days
  • infection requiring IV antibiotics within 28 days
  • fever or illness within 14 days of dosing
  • major surgery within 12 weeks of screening or planned surgery
  • history of small intestine or bariatric surgery or other surgical treatments for obesity
  • known abnormal heart rhythm
  • history of diabetes (previous gestational is fine)
  • cancer within 5 years (BCC/SCC and CIN okay if > 2 years ago)
  • any history of melanoma
  • history of seizures
  • HIV, Hep B, Hep C
  • history of sensitivity to heparin or heparin-induced thrombocytopenia

elements.name: question20
elements.title: Before we wrap up, I’d like to share details about our referral program. If you refer someone to us you can receive up to $250 if they enrol and participate in the study. Would you like to hear more?

elements.name: question21
elements.html:
Great! Here's how it works:

 

To refer someone, you will need to provide them with a unique referral ID. The person you refer will need to provide us this ID either when they sign up on our website, or when they speak to us over the phone. This ID is essential, as it ensures we can track and reimburse you for any referrals.

 

For each person you refer who comes in for an in-person screening visit, you'll receive $50. If they go on to enrol and participate in the study, you'll earn an additional $200.

 

There's no limit- you can refer as many people as you'd like, as long as you have an exisiting relationship with them. It's important to note that you cannot advertise for referrals. This program is based on personal connections, so please only refer people you know.

 

If you're interested, we can set up your Unique Referral ID today if you would like (the unique referral ID is REF[p number]. E.g., REFP14471)

 

Who do you know you might be interested in this trial? (if they don't know anyone for this trial, they can also refer someone to any other trial)

 

Would you like us to send you an email that you can forward on to them?
